sections.title: Organizational Processes & Documentation
sections.content:
Operations run on documentation and change control.
Change management — a formal process to request, review, approve, test, and roll back changes, with a maintenance window and rollback plan. Prevents 'cowboy' changes that cause outages.
Configuration management — track known-good configs, baselines, and versioning so you can detect drift and restore.
Key documents: physical & logical network diagrams, rack diagrams, IP address management (IPAM), asset inventory, and a wiring/port map.
Policies & agreements: SLA (service-level agreement — uptime/response commitments), MOU, NDA, AUP (acceptable use), and a BYOD policy. Site documentation plus a runbook speeds recovery.
exam_tips: Change management = request → approve → scheduled window → implement → rollback plan.
An SLA defines uptime/response commitments between provider and customer.
Keep both physical and logical network diagrams current; use IPAM for addressing.

sections.title: Network Monitoring
sections.content:
You can't manage what you don't measure.
SNMP — polls devices for status (interfaces, CPU, errors); devices send traps on events (UDP 161/162). SNMPv3 adds authentication + encryption.
Syslog — centralizes log messages (UDP 514), rated by severity (0 emergency … 7 debug).
Flow data — NetFlow/sFlow/IPFIX report who-talked-to-whom and how much, for traffic analysis and baselining.
SIEM — aggregates and correlates logs/alerts for security.
Establish a baseline of normal performance (throughput, latency, utilization) so anomalies stand out. Track metrics: bandwidth/utilization, latency, jitter, packet loss, and error/discard counters. Use dashboards and alerting thresholds.
exam_tips: SNMP polls + traps for device health (use v3 for security); Syslog centralizes logs (severity 0–7).
NetFlow/sFlow show traffic flows (top talkers/conversations), not packet contents.
Baseline normal performance first so you can spot anomalies later.

sections.title: Disaster Recovery & High Availability
sections.content:
Plan for failure.
Key metrics: RTO (Recovery Time Objective — how fast you must be back) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective — how much data loss is tolerable, i.e., backup frequency). MTTR (mean time to repair) and MTBF (mean time between failures) describe reliability.
Site types: hot site (fully running, instant failover), warm site (equipment ready, some setup), cold site (space/power only, slowest). 
High availability: redundancy (N+1), failover clustering, load balancing, FHRP (first-hop redundancy — VRRP/HSRP) so hosts keep a working default gateway.
Backups: full/incremental/differential; follow 3-2-1 (3 copies, 2 media, 1 offsite) and test restores.
exam_tips: RTO = how fast you recover; RPO = how much data you can afford to lose (drives backup frequency).
Hot site = instant failover; cold site = space/power only (slowest, cheapest).
FHRP (VRRP/HSRP) provides a redundant default gateway for high availability.

concept_cards.hook: A formal process to request, approve, schedule, implement, and roll back network changes to avoid unplanned outages.
Service-Level Agreement — a contract defining guaranteed uptime, performance, and response times between a provider and customer.
Simple Network Management Protocol — polls devices for health data and receives traps on events; use v3 for authentication and encryption.
A recorded sample of normal performance (throughput, latency, utilization) used as a reference to detect anomalies.
Records of traffic conversations (source, destination, volume) used to see top talkers and analyze usage — not packet contents.
Recovery Time Objective is how quickly service must be restored; Recovery Point Objective is the maximum tolerable data loss, which sets backup frequency.
Disaster-recovery sites by readiness: hot (fully running, instant), warm (equipment staged), cold (space and power only).
First-Hop Redundancy Protocols that present a virtual default gateway so hosts stay reachable if one router fails.

practice_questions.q: Which document records the step-by-step procedure to restore a specific service after failure?
practice_questions.explanation: A runbook holds the operational steps to recover or operate a service; an SLA defines commitments, not steps.

practice_questions.q: Which protocol centralizes device log messages to a collector, rated by severity 0–7?
practice_questions.explanation: Syslog sends event messages (severity 0 emergency to 7 debug) to a central server, usually UDP 514.

practice_questions.q: Which metric defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, driving backup frequency?
practice_questions.explanation: The Recovery Point Objective sets how much data loss is tolerable, which determines how often you back up.

practice_questions.q: Before a planned core-switch upgrade, which practice ensures you can revert if it fails?
options: Back up the current config and document a rollback plan
practice_questions.explanation: Configuration management + a documented rollback plan let you restore the known-good config if the change goes wrong.

options: To recognize abnormal behavior by comparing against normal
practice_questions.explanation: A baseline of normal metrics lets you spot anomalies and degradation later.

practice_questions.q: A recovery facility is fully equipped and running for near-instant failover. What is it?
practice_questions.explanation: A hot site mirrors production and can take over almost immediately.

practice_questions.q: What is the purpose of a formal change-management process?
options: Review, approve, and schedule changes with a rollback plan to avoid outages
Let any admin change configs instantly
practice_questions.explanation: Change management controls how changes are requested, approved, implemented, and rolled back.

practice_questions.q: Which tool shows top talkers and traffic conversations (not packet contents)?
practice_questions.explanation: Flow data (NetFlow/sFlow) reports source, destination, and volume of conversations.

practice_questions.q: Which protocol provides a redundant default gateway so hosts stay reachable if a router fails?
practice_questions.explanation: First-Hop Redundancy Protocols present a virtual gateway IP shared by redundant routers.

practice_questions.q: Which document defines the uptime and response commitments between a provider and customer?
practice_questions.explanation: A Service-Level Agreement specifies guaranteed availability and response times.
